variables.title: Authentication rejection investigation
variables.query: event.outcome: failure and authentication.rejection_reason: * and not authentication.rejection_reason: ${param.incident.noise_reason_a}

drifts.note: You filtered on the rejection reason ${action.value}; check whether it's the one that is surging rather than background noise.

demonstration.narration: Routine sign-in rejections are mixed with the spike. I'll keep failed requests with a reason and exclude the routine one so the unusual reason stands out.
demonstration.reasoning: The current window contains normal and background events. Filtering on ${var.field} reduces that noise so we can inspect the relevant records.
demonstration.evidence: The result table now shows records matching the query. Read the ${var.field} values and neighbouring fields to identify the pattern; a single record will provide a further check.

demonstration.narration: I'll open one unusual rejection to see its reason and affected client in the same request.
demonstration.reasoning: A total can look convincing even when it includes an unrelated record. Opening a typical event checks the key values together, rather than relying on a count alone.
demonstration.evidence: The opened event connects ${truth.finding} with ${truth.scope}. Together, this record and the filtered results support the conclusion: ${truth.conclusion}
